title: Fidget Pie
subtitle: A Shropshire harvest pie of bacon, apple, and onion under a shortcrust lid
excerpt: Back bacon, sharp cooking apple, and onion layered in a shortcrust case with a little cider and sage. An old West Midlands harvest-time pie with a good balance of salt and sweet-tart fruit.
sourceNotes: Fidget pie comes from Shropshire and Worcestershire; traditionally eaten during the apple harvest, this version follows the layered construction recorded in British regional cookery sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pie the day before, keep it unbaked in the fridge, and bake on the day. Add 5 minutes to the baking time.

content.text: Fidget pie is a layered, unfussy thing: bacon and apple with a little onion, a splash of cider, and a shortcrust lid. Use a proper cooking apple, not a dessert variety, or the filling will be too sweet. The cider keeps the filling moist as it bakes without making it wet.

items.prepNote: to dust over the filling layers

content.text: Heat the oven to 190C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line a 20cm deep pie dish. Leave a 2cm overhang. Chill for 20 minutes.

Layer half the bacon over the pastry base. Top with half the apple slices and half the onion. Scatter over half the sage and a light dusting of flour. Season with black pepper. Repeat the layers with the remaining bacon, apple, onion, and sage.
Pour the cider over the filling. It should come about halfway up the layers.
Roll the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the pastry rim with beaten egg. Lay the lid over the filling and press firmly to seal. Trim and crimp the edges.
Brush the top with beaten egg. Cut a small slit in the centre to let the steam out.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is cooked through. Cover with foil if the top colours too quickly.
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing. The pie is good hot or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The cider has made the bottom pastry soggy.
items.cause: Too much liquid in the filling, or the base was not pre-chilled.
items.fix: Dust each layer generously with flour to absorb the juices. Chill the assembled pie for 20 minutes before baking.

items.symptom: The lid has sunk into the filling.
items.cause: The apple and onion collapsed during baking and the filling reduced too much.
items.fix: Layer the apple slightly proud of the rim so the filling supports the lid as it cooks down.

items.symptom: The bacon is still chewy and pale inside.
items.cause: The oven temperature was too low or the pie was underbaked.
items.fix: Bake at a steady 190C for the full 50 minutes; the lid should be deep golden, not pale, before removing.
